narration_script: 60 frames per second can still feel stuttery. The number is real, but it does not tell you when each frame arrived. FPS is an average across time. Smoothness also lives in the gaps, the rhythm between one finished frame and the next. At a clean 60, a new image arrives about every 16 .7 milliseconds, tick, tick, tick, and even visual cadence. Now let one frame take 40 milliseconds. Faster frames can pull the average back up, yet your eye still catches that single pause. that is uneven frame pacing. The engine, driver and display must hand frames over steadily, not merely finish 60 somewhere inside a second. So when a game feels rough, watch the frame time graph as well as the FPS counter. The average can hide the hitch.
